page.title: Investor relations event production guide
page.description: Learn the first decisions, owners, platforms, rehearsals and deliverables for earnings calls, investor days, AGMs and LP updates.
page.h1: Investor relations event production: what to decide first
page.definition: Investor relations event production is the end‑to‑end planning and live execution of earnings calls, investor days, annual general meetings and limited‑partner updates, covering platform selection, run‑of‑show ownership, speaker rehearsals, backup streams and post‑event deliverables such as edited recordings and compliance‑ready clips.
page.quick_answer: Start by naming the event type, assigning a single run‑of‑show owner, and locking the streaming platform at least six weeks before the date. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: What event types fall under investor relations production?

blocks.p: Investor relations production covers earnings calls, investor days, annual general meetings and limited‑partner updates, each with distinct compliance and audience requirements.

ul: Earnings call – quarterly results, live Q&A, regulatory filing deadline
Investor day – deep‑dive presentations, multiple speakers, breakout sessions
Annual general meeting – shareholder voting, proxy reporting, legal record
Limited‑partner update – fund performance, capital calls, confidential data handling

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and key decisions?

blocks.p: A single producer owns the run of show, while separate leads handle speaker management, platform operation and compliance review to keep the broadcast on track.

ul: Producer – owns run of show, cues, timing, backup stream
Speaker manager – briefs presenters, collects slides, runs rehearsals
Platform operator – configures streaming settings, monitors ingest, switches backup
Compliance lead – verifies disclosure language, records retention, audit trail

sections.h2: Which platform and production model should I choose?

blocks.p: Choose a platform that matches audience size, compliance needs and internal workflow, then pair it with a production crew that supplies cameras, encoders and a backup stream.

sections.h2: What rehearsals and backup plans are required?

blocks.p: Run one full rehearsal on the live platform two to five days before the event and a technical check sixty minutes before go‑live, with a standby backup stream ready.

ol: Schedule full rehearsal with all speakers and production crew
Test slides, lower thirds, Q&A flow and backup encoder
Confirm compliance disclaimer timing and recording start
Execute sixty‑minute technical check, verify audio, video and failover
Go live with producer cueing and moderator standing by

sections.h2: What deliverables and timelines should I expect?

blocks.p: Deliverables include a run of show, speaker briefs, branded slides, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips, delivered within three to four weeks for a webinar or six to eight weeks for a summit.

ul: Run of show document with cue timestamps
Branded slide template and lower thirds

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a hybrid investor day?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid investor day six to eight weeks ahead to secure venue AV, lock the streaming platform and finalize the agenda before speaker briefs are sent. Allow extra time for compliance review, backup stream testing and post‑event transcript preparation.

faq.q: What compliance checks are needed for earnings call recordings?
faq.a: Verify that all forward‑looking statements carry the required safe‑harbor language, confirm the recording meets SEC retention rules, and ensure the transcript is time‑stamped for audit purposes. Also archive the backup stream and distribute the approved version to legal and investor‑relations teams within twenty‑four hours.

faq.q: Can I use my existing Zoom Webinars licence for an investor day?
faq.a: Yes, if the licence covers the expected attendee capacity and includes webinar‑level reporting, you can run the investor day on Zoom Webinars while a production crew handles cameras, encoders and a backup stream. Confirm that the plan supports simultaneous interpretation and Q&A moderation features required for compliance.

faq.q: What is the typical cost range for a moderated webinar production?
faq.a: Moderated webinars: $2,500 to $7,500 per production, covering producer, speaker rehearsal, branded graphics, live Q&A moderation, backup stream and edited recording delivery. The fee also includes a compliance‑ready transcript and a highlight clip package for investor‑relations distribution. Travel and venue costs are excluded and quoted separately.
